# Pluggable

A part Danbyte seats in a port or a rack unit, in `danbyte/pluggables/<Vendor>/<NAME>.yaml` (a pack's `accessory-types/`): transceivers, plugs and cords (export spec §13), and rack parts: blanking panels, cable managers, shelves (§14). Danbyte draws the part at a port's `port:` anchor while the port is cabled or a transceiver is recorded in it, and picks one by `fits` (the port type), `parts` (the recorded part number) and `connector` (the cable's medium).

Schema: [`danbyte/schema/pluggable.schema.json`](../../schema/pluggable.schema.json) (danbyte-library/v1).

Files: `danbyte/pluggables/<Vendor>/<NAME>.yaml`. Start each with the editor line, so VS Code (YAML extension) completes and checks keys as you type:

```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=<relative path to>/danbyte/schema/pluggable.schema.json
```

## Keys

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `format` | [format](common.md#format) |  | The library format this file is written for. Optional; the tools write it, and a later format will change the value. |
| `name` | string | yes | The part's name: the vendor part number for a real part (`SFP-10G-SR`), the common name in capitals for a generic one (`RJ45-PLUG`). Equals the file name. |
| `kind` | one of `transceiver`, `plug`, `cord`, `blanking`, `cable-manager`, `shelf` | yes | transceiver (a module in a cage, with a `port:<connector>` empty a cord seats in), plug or cord (a cable end; cord = one-piece parts such as DACs and stack cables), or a rack part: blanking, cable-manager, shelf. |
| `connector` | string (pattern) |  | The connector it presents or is: `rj45`, `lc`, `sc`, `mpo`, `c13` / `c15` / `c19` (IEC cords), `dac` / `aoc` (one-piece cables), `stack` (stack cable heads, chosen by `fits`). Danbyte groups parts by medium from it: lc/sc/mpo… fibre, dac/twinax DAC, rj45 copper. A cord seats at a transceiver's `port:<connector>` empty when the connectors match. |
| `fits` | list of string (pattern) |  | The port types (NetBox interface, console or power port type slugs, or Danbyte extension types such as `cisco-stackpower`) it plugs into. Required for every kind but rack parts. |
| `parts` | list of [partNumber](common.md#partnumber) |  | Every vendor part number this model stands for, as printed on the label and as switches report them (`SFP-10G-SR`, not `SFP-10G-SR=`; a trailing `=` is ignored). Empty for a generic fallback. |
| `standard` | string |  | The IEEE / MSA name (`10GBASE-SR`, `100GBASE-SR4`, `1000BASE-T`), or the stack system for stack cables. |
| `wavelength_nm` | integer (1–100000) |  | Nominal wavelength in nm; leave it out for copper. |
| `reach_m` | number (…–200000) |  | Nominal reach in metres. |
| `u_height` | integer (0–10) |  | Rack parts only: height in rack units, 0 for a vertical (0U) part such as a 2-post vertical cable manager. (Danbyte's importer in 0.21 takes 1-10 and refuses 0.) |
| `cable` | [cable](#cable) |  | How Danbyte draws a cord's run from its `cable` empty to the other end (export spec §13): one round jacket, a zip cord (two side by side) or a ribbon (several side by side, along the empty's local X), with corners no tighter than the minimum bend radius where there is room. |
| `comments` | string |  | What the model shows and where its sizes come from. |
| `model3d` | mapping | yes | The part's model: origin where the plug meets the port, +Z out of the port, +Y up; a cord's run continues from its `cable` empty. Budgets: transceiver ≤ 1,500 triangles, plug or cord ≤ 2,000, rack part ≤ 5,000; ≤ 200 KB (rack parts ≤ 8 MB). No far copy. |
| `meta` | [meta](meta.md) |  | Catalog facts (see meta); category `pluggable`. |

### model3d

The part's model: origin where the plug meets the port, +Z out of the port, +Y up; a cord's run continues from its `cable` empty. Budgets: transceiver ≤ 1,500 triangles, plug or cord ≤ 2,000, rack part ≤ 5,000; ≤ 200 KB (rack parts ≤ 8 MB). No far copy.

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | [glbPath](common.md#glbpath) | yes | A binary glTF 2.0 file (`.glb`) under `danbyte/`, normally `assets/<Vendor>/<PART>.glb`. Stored with Git LFS. |

Example:

```yaml
name: SFP-10G-SR
kind: transceiver
connector: lc
fits: [10gbase-x-sfpp]
parts: [SFP-10G-SR, SFP-10G-SR-S]
standard: 10GBASE-SR
wavelength_nm: 850
model3d: {file: assets/Cisco/SFP-10G-SR.glb}
meta: {category: pluggable}
```

## Definitions

### cable

How Danbyte draws a cord's run from its `cable` empty to the other end (export spec §13): one round jacket, a zip cord (two side by side) or a ribbon (several side by side, along the empty's local X), with corners no tighter than the minimum bend radius where there is room.

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `profile` | one of `round`, `zipcord`, `ribbon` | yes | round, zipcord (two jackets) or ribbon (count jackets). |
| `count` | integer (2–8) |  | Ribbon only: how many jackets. |
| `jacket_mm` | number (…–50) | yes | Jacket diameter, mm. |
| `pitch_mm` | number (…–100) |  | Zip cord and ribbon: centre to centre, mm; no narrower than the jacket. |
| `min_bend_mm` | number (…–2000) |  | Minimum bend radius, mm (the default for every length). |
| `min_bend_by_part` | map of name → number (…–2000) |  | Part number → minimum bend radius (mm), where one length needs more than `min_bend_mm`. Keys should be listed in `parts`. |

Example:

```yaml
profile: ribbon
count: 3
pitch_mm: 11.2
jacket_mm: 6.1
min_bend_mm: 41
min_bend_by_part: {STACK-T1-3M: 82}
```
